blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Delete control is a clickable div unreachable by keyboard) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-accessibility-2 (Icon-only delete control has no accessible name) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Render the delete control as a native `<button type="button" className="icon-button" onClick={onDelete}>`. The `div` has no role, no `tabindex` and no key handler: a keyboard user pressing Tab never lands on it, and Enter or Space cannot trigger it, so the change's one purpose — deleting a document from its page — cannot be completed without a mouse. Screen readers also announce it as plain text, not as a button. WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.
findings.title: Delete control is a clickable div unreachable by keyboard

findings.recommendation: Give the control a text name, e.g. `aria-label="Delete document"` on the button (and `aria-hidden="true"` on the decorative `TrashIcon` SVG), or visually hidden text inside it. As written, the only content is an icon: a screen reader user reaching the control hears nothing that says it deletes the document, so they cannot identify the action. Making it a `<button>` (R-accessibility-1) does not supply a name by itself. WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.
findings.title: Icon-only delete control has no accessible name

findings.recommendation: Add an `alt` naming the owner, e.g. `alt={`${ownerName}'s avatar`}` or `alt={ownerName}` (the component needs the owner's name as a prop). The avatar conveys who owns the document; without `alt`, screen readers read the image URL or file name instead, so screen reader users do not learn who the owner is. If the owner is shown in text elsewhere, use `alt=""` to mark it decorative. WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content.
findings.title: Owner avatar image has no alt text

findings.recommendation: The `.icon-button` stylesheet is not part of the change. Once the control is a focusable button, check that it shows a visible focus indicator (no `outline: none` without replacement, WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible) and that its target is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels or spaced accordingly (WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)).
findings.title: Focus style and target size of the icon button not visible in the change
